task: Draft a case-study background section (three paragraphs: organisation overview, onboarding challenge, and implementation scope) for a fictional HR-software product. Use only the supplied facts. Do not add outcome claims, cost savings, employee survey results, or quantified productivity data not in the facts.

facts.text: The fictional HR software is called PeopleAxis.
A fictional professional-services firm, Dunhill Consulting Group, employs approximately 240 people across four offices.
Dunhill's technology practice manages the onboarding programme for all new professional staff.
In 2024 Dunhill hired a cohort of 90 new professionals across all four offices in a compressed eight-week period.
The onboarding process involves tasks managed across IT, HR, and compliance teams.
Each new hire was assigned a named onboarding coordinator responsible for tracking their task completion.
Dunhill used PeopleAxis to assign tasks, track deadlines, and share document checklists during the cohort onboarding.
The implementation covered a six-month period in 2024, including an initial configuration phase.
The case study does not report quantified productivity, cost, or time-to-productivity data.

forbidden_additions: Quantified productivity or cost savings not in the facts.
An employee satisfaction rating or time-to-productivity figure.
A claim that PeopleAxis reduced turnover or improved performance scores.
preserve: The 240-employee firm size and four-office structure.
The 90-person cohort hired in a compressed eight-week period.
The cross-team scope: IT, HR, and compliance.
The named-coordinator model and the six-month 2024 implementation period.
